items.t: PGE stock: Rybnik project secures PLN 3.886 billion loan
sum: PGE Polska Grupa Energetyczna signed a PLN 3.886 billion term loan on Thursday, November 5, 2026, for its gas-and-steam power project in Rybnik. AD HOC NEWS reported the agreement based on information from PAP as published by nettg.pl.

The loan was arranged by PKO BP, BGK, Erste Bank Polska and Bank Pekao. Poland's export credit insurer KUKE guarantees the financing, which is intended to fund or refinance investment spending for the combined-cycle gas turbine block.

The Rybnik unit has an electrical capacity of 882 megawatts. PGE said final installation and construction work is under way, while individual systems are being transferred progressively for commissioning. Chemical cleaning of boiler systems and steam pipelines is also being prepared.

The company expects the gas turbine to fire for the first time and the unit to synchronize with Poland's national power system around the turn of 2026 and 2027. The schedule creates a near-term execution milestone for a project designed to add more flexible and lower-carbon generation.

PGE Chief Executive Dariusz Lubera has described gas generation as a key pillar of the updated strategy. The company is developing or preparing gas projects with combined capacity above 5 gigawatts and aims to reach about 8 gigawatts of gas capacity by 2035, or 9.6 gigawatts including gas units in district heating.

PGE stock traded at 3.58 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 18:02 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026. The quote was 2.45 percent below the 3.67 euros reported in the previous relevant article at 12:06:40 CET on Thursday, November 5.

Investors can follow the real-time quote of PGE Polska Grupa Energetyczna stock. The financing strengthens visibility on the Rybnik build-out but also highlights the capital commitments and borrowing required for PGE's transition.

items.t: WIG 20 closes 0.46 percent higher at 4,209.15 points
sum: The WIG 20 ended Thursday's session at 4,209.15 points, up 0.46 percent from the previous close, according to ISBnews. The close followed a second consecutive advance for Warsaw's blue-chip index, but the wider market moved in the opposite direction: the WIG fell 0.07 percent, while the mWIG40 and sWIG80 declined 1.62 percent and 1.00 percent, respectively.

Selected consumer companies and banks provided the main support. A WNP report citing PAP said LPP, Dino Polska and Modivo were among the stronger consumer names during the session. LPP had reported estimated third-quarter sales growth of 20 percent in constant currencies, while comparable-store sales increased 4.4 percent.

Bank stocks also contributed to the advance. PKO BP rose after reporting third-quarter 2026 net profit of PLN 2,933 million, up from PLN 2,837 million a year earlier and 4.1 percent above analysts' expectations, according to the same report. Selected other banks also gained, although the sector's performance remained mixed.

The positive performance of the WIG 20 did not reflect the broader trading session. ISBnews reported that 113 stocks rose on the Warsaw Stock Exchange, 220 declined and 69 were unchanged. Within the blue-chip index, KGHM and Allegro were among the notable decliners. KGHM fell after returning to losses, while Allegro also weakened following a strong run in previous weeks.

Energy shares were mixed to firmer in the session. PGE and Tauron gained, while PGE also announced a PLN 3.89 billion term-loan agreement with a banking consortium to finance or refinance investment spending related to a gas-fired power plant in Rybnik. This company-specific development was reported in the market coverage and is not, by itself, evidence of a broader index trend.

The WNP report quoted Noble Securities analyst Mateusz Chrzanowski as linking the improved mood in Warsaw to greater risk appetite after the US elections and to easing concerns about risks connected with the Iran conflict. He also pointed to lower commodity prices and their possible effect on inflation expectations. At the same time, the report noted that expectations for lower interest-rate pressure could offset some of the benefit for banks.

WIG 20 closes at 4,152.65 points after volatile session
sum: The WIG 20 ended the Warsaw session on Monday, November 2, at 4,152.65 points, down 0.68 percent from the previous close. The closing level and daily change were reported in the Warsaw Stock Exchange data release published by Strefa Inwestorow.

The session was marked by pronounced intraday volatility. According to Bankier.pl, selling pressure pushed the index to about 4,108 points at around 15:30, equivalent to a 1.78 percent decline at that point. Demand returned late in the session and helped reduce the loss before the close. The broader WIG fell 0.82 percent, while the mWIG40 dropped 1.45 percent and the sWIG80 lost 0.95 percent.

Financial companies were the most significant source of pressure within the blue-chip index. Bank Pekao fell 3.35 percent, PKO BP declined 1.94 percent, Erste Bank lost 1.80 percent and mBank decreased 0.77 percent, according to Bankier.pl. Other notable decliners included Pepco, down 2.87 percent, Tauron, down 2.86 percent, PGE, down 2.52 percent, Kruk, down 2 percent, and Orlen, down 1.42 percent.

The late recovery was broad enough to leave 11 of the 20 WIG 20 constituents higher by the close. KGHM led the gainers with a 2.22 percent increase, followed by Budimex at 1.42 percent. LPP rose 0.97 percent and Allegro gained 0.76 percent.

Bankier.pl reported that the decline in Warsaw contrasted with gains in several major overseas markets. Analysts cited renewed political risk linked to the dispute around Poland's Constitutional Tribunal, particularly ahead of a scheduled S&P rating review on Friday. The article also pointed to weaker-than-expected October inflation, which reduced market expectations for possible interest-rate increases and weighed on the outlook for banks' net interest margins. These factors provide context for the session's weakness, but do not by themselves establish a single cause for the index move.
For further coverage of the index, visit the WIG 20 topic page.

items.t: Raiffeisen Bank stock heads into key third-quarter results
sum: Raiffeisen Bank International is scheduled to release its third-quarter 2026 results on Tuesday, November 3, according to an AD HOC NEWS report published on October 26. The release will give investors the first major earnings checkpoint of the week.

Raiffeisen Bank reported second-quarter 2026 net income of EUR 754.0 million, compared with a EUR 586.0 million loss in the second quarter of 2025. The result marked a sharp change in profitability and provides the main operating benchmark for the upcoming report.

Analyst activity has added another reference point. Autonomous Research raised its target for Raiffeisen Bank International from EUR 67.35 to EUR 67.52 on October 16 while keeping a Neutral recommendation, according to the cited report. Other October target changes included a EUR 67.00 target from PKO BP Securities and a EUR 57.00 target from Keefe Bruyette & Woods.
Raiffeisen Bank stock traded at EUR 55.78 on Lang & Schwarz at 5:15 p.m. CET on Sunday, November 1, 2026; the real-time quote of Raiffeisen Bank stock is available through the stock page.
Austria's ATX provides the relevant market backdrop for the Vienna-listed bank as investors position for the earnings release.

items.t: When Will Vincent Kompany Return? Bayern Munich Shares Health Update
sum: Aaron Danks has confirmed that Vincent Kompany is out of the hospital, but there is still no timetable for his return. Bayern Munich are giving their head coach all the time he needs to recover.… Show More

Aaron Danks, assistant coach at Bayern Munich, has confirmed that Vincent Kompany has been discharged from the hospital and is continuing his recovery, although there is still no timetable for his return. Danks stressed that the Belgian's health comes first and that Bayern will give him as much time as he needs before returning to the sidelines. In the meantime, Danks will lead the team as the German giants look to maintain their strong form across the Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal and UEFA Champions League.

items.t: WIG 20 closes 1.0 percent higher as banks lead
sum: WIG 20 closed 40 points, or 1.0 percent, higher at 4,238 points on October 27, 2026. Bank earnings lifted the benchmark as Polish lenders led the advance.
mBank was the strongest WIG 20 stock, rising 4.7 percent before its third-quarter results. Since the midday level of 4,212 points, WIG 20 added 26 points, or 0.6 percent.
The WIG Banks index climbed 3.1 percent, according to Parkiet. Better-than-expected quarterly results from Alior Bank and Bank Millennium supported their shares and spread through the banking sector.
The broader market also finished higher, with 160 stocks rising and 161 falling on the Warsaw exchange, according to Investing.com.
- Alior Bank up 3.4 percent: quarterly results beat expectations.

WIG 20 ended below its October 21 closing record of 4,267 points, while the banking sector supplied the session's main support. The index's 40-point gain represented a rebound from the 4,198-point close on October 26.

items.t: WIG 20 falls 1.3 percent as banks and KGHM slide
sum: WIG 20 was down 54 points, or 1.3 percent, at 4,213 points at 12:02 p.m. CEST on October 22, 2026, as banks and KGHM weakened. Polish retail sales rose 3.3 percent year over year in September, below the 6.9 percent consensus, XTB reported.

Since the 4,168-point midday level, WIG 20 has recovered 45 points. Pepco rose 1.6 percent after the company announced a new multiyear share-buyback program, while KGHM remained the weakest blue chip, PAP reported.

Bank stocks and energy shares were among the weakest groups in Warsaw. KGHM fell 2.8 percent, while PKO BP and Pekao each lost about 2.0 percent, according to PAP. The selling followed Wednesday's record close, when WIG 20 reached 4,267 points.
- Pepco up 1.6 percent: shares advanced after a new buyback program was announced.
- KGHM down 2.8 percent: the copper producer extended its recent decline.
- PKO BP down 2.0 percent: bank shares weakened with the sector.
- Pekao down 2.0 percent: the stock followed the broader bank-sector decline.

Poland’s WIG20 stock market index hits record high
sum: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!

Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support.
Poland’s blue-chip WIG20 stock market index hit its highest ever level on Monday, surpassing a record that had stood for almost 19 years.

The WIG20 has been Europe’s best-performing major blue-chip index so far this year. According to market monitoring website MarketScreener, the index has gained just under 25% since the start of 2026, ahead of the Dutch AEX (16.9%) and Sweden’s OMX Stockholm (14.9%).

The WIG20, which tracks the 20 largest and most liquid companies on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (GPW), climbed to 3,963.21 points on Monday, breaking its previous record of 3,940.53 points set in October 2007. It continues a rally that began in October 2022, since when the index has almost tripled in value.

“The market continues to be supported by solid economic growth, rising consumer spending, and the prospect of further EU investment,” commented analysts from BNP Paribas, a bank, quoted by business daily Parkiet.
“However, after such strong gains, we do not expect the pace of appreciation to remain as high as in recent years,” they added.
